_metadata.rubric: x02 rubric (owner style examples, clicks-when-explained bar, fewer phrase-joins, mechanism labelled, explanation checked), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: Apart from the instructions file, I read only x02-e-review-input.json and opened no other file, repository search, web page or API.

hints.reason: DONKEY via Nintendo's Donkey Kong and GODZILLA via the Godzilla vs. Kong film rivalry; one giant-ape name joins a video game and a monster movie.

best_available.why: Instant on both sides, and pairing an arcade ape with a monster-movie rival is fun.

pairs.pair_note: Ideal pair; nothing to change.

hints.reason: CARPET via Aladdin's magic carpet and LAMP via the Genie's lamp; one story covers both.

best_available.why: The most natural hint possible for these two words.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair. Not a surprise, but it is the right hint.

hints.reason: LADY via Lady Gaga and QUEEN via the band's "Radio Ga Ga," which gave her the name; the Queen side takes a beat but lands as a real 'oh, nice'.

best_available.why: A true name-origin fact that joins a pop star to a rock band.

pairs.pair_note: Most players will get QUEEN via "Radio Ga Ga" even if they don't know the name-origin story.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via the midnight clock and CROCODILE via Peter Pan's ticking crocodile that swallowed a clock; two famous story scenes.

best_available.why: Two iconic storybook clocks; it clicks right away.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. This is the story-based style the owner wants more of.

hints.reason: NOODLE via eating with chopsticks and PIANO via the beginner tune "Chopsticks"; a clean double meaning.

best_available.why: A real double meaning that both sides grasp immediately.

pairs.pair_note: One of the batch's best.

hints.reason: PENCIL via graphite "lead" and DIAMOND via both being forms of carbon; the diamond side needs basic science, but most players will accept it once it is explained.

best_available.why: A true and fairly well-known chemistry fact; the pencil side guides the solve.

pairs.pair_note: The diamond side is the weaker one, but the idea is sound and the explanation is accurate.

hints.reason: ARCHITECTURE via Frank Lloyd Wright and PLANE via the Wright brothers; one surname, two famous American pioneers.

best_available.why: Two famous people share one name, which makes a satisfying reveal.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent. Labelled double_meaning because two different people share the name.

hints.reason: OPERA via The Phantom of the Opera and STAR WARS via The Phantom Menace; it is a title-word join, but both titles are instantly familiar and the pairing is satisfying, so it clears the exceptional bar.

best_available.why: Two blockbuster titles share one word, and the Opera side is a real character.

pairs.pair_note: A title-word join that qualifies as exceptional. The facts are correct: Episode I is The Phantom Menace.

hints.reason: SKATEBOARD via Tony Hawk and TIGER via Tony the Tiger; two famous Tonys.

best_available.why: Two household Tonys; it's playful and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pop-culture pair.

hints.reason: ELVIS via his Vegas legacy and impersonators, and WEDDING via quickie Vegas chapels; the Elvis-officiated chapel wedding brings both together.

best_available.why: One vivid scene contains both targets.

pairs.pair_note: The combined-idea explanation is a good example of the style.

hints.reason: ELECTRICITY via electric current and RIVER via a river's current; a textbook double meaning.

best_available.why: The perfect natural hint for this pair.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and familiar rather than surprising, but correct.

hints.reason: HAMMER via Mjolnir and THUNDER via Thor being the god of thunder; one character covers both.

best_available.why: Obvious, but it is the natural hint.

pairs.pair_note: Easy solve.

hints.reason: FATHER via "I am your father" and HAND via Vader cutting off Luke's hand in the same Empire Strikes Back duel; one famous scene.

best_available.why: Both targets come from the same iconic duel.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent scene-based hint; the facts are correct.

hints.reason: CHIMNEY via Bert's chimney sweeps ("Step in Time") and PENGUIN via the cartoon penguin waiters in "Jolly Holiday"; the penguin side is a little less famous but clicks once mentioned.

best_available.why: Two memorable scenes from one beloved film.

pairs.pair_note: The facts are accurate. The penguin side is the softer one.

hints.reason: CRICKET via Jiminy Cricket and WHALE via Monstro; one Disney story covers both.

best_available.why: One story, two famous creatures.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: SANTA via the Grinch's Santa disguise and THIEF via his stealing Christmas; one story, both sides.

best_available.why: The Santa-suit thief is exactly what both words point to.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: TOOTH via the narwhal's tusk being a tooth and UNICORN via its nickname "unicorn of the sea"; a great fact.
hints.fix: Drop the false cause-and-effect: "A narwhal's spiral 'horn' is really a long tooth, and it earns the narwhal the nickname unicorn of the sea." (The nickname comes from the horn-like look, not from it being a tooth.)

best_available.why: A delightful true fact that covers both words.

pairs.pair_note: Only the explanation's 'which is why' needs a light edit.

hints.reason: DYNAMITE via Alfred Nobel inventing it and EINSTEIN via his 1921 Nobel Prize; the irony of dynamite funding a prize makes it satisfying.

best_available.why: True on both sides, with a nice surprise on the dynamite side.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: ELVIS via Graceland in Memphis is instant, but PYRAMID via ancient Egypt's Memphis depends on geography most U.S. players don't know, so the pyramid side is the weak one.
hints.fix: Add the U.S. hook: "Elvis's Graceland is in Memphis, which has its own giant Pyramid arena and is named after the ancient Egyptian capital near the pyramids."

best_available.why: Clever two-Memphis idea; it works best if the explanation also mentions the Memphis Pyramid in Tennessee.

pairs.pair_note: The idea is good, but the pyramid side is soft. Mentioning Memphis's own Pyramid arena could push it to PASS.

hints.reason: TORNADO via the Kansas twister (and tornado country) and WIZARD via The Wizard of Oz's "not in Kansas anymore"; one story covers both.

best_available.why: Natural and fair; there is no setting more fitting for this pair.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: DUCK via down feathers and FOOTBALL via downs; a clean double meaning with a nice misdirect.

best_available.why: A crisp double meaning that hides well on a board.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: ANGEL via Charlie's Angels and FOOTBALL via Lucy pulling the football away from Charlie Brown; two famous Charlies, and the Peanuts gag is a lovely reveal.

best_available.why: The Charlie Brown football gag makes it a real 'oh, nice'.

pairs.pair_note: The Angel side reads as a title join, but the football side is a scene, so overall it is a two-Charlies double reference.

hints.reason: ARM via the upper-arm bone and FUNNY via the 'humorous' pun (and the funny-bone joke); a classic, beloved pun.

best_available.why: A well-known pun that fits the pair perfectly.

pairs.pair_note: Optionally, the explanation could also mention the funny bone.

hints.reason: EAR via Dumbo's huge ears and FLY via his flying with them; one character, one image.

best_available.why: A single image that combines both words.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: DOOR via knocking on a door and JOKE via the knock-knock joke; the joke side is a compound, but it is instantly familiar and the joke itself pretends to knock at a door, so it passes as exceptional.
hints.fix: Make it one idea rather than circular: "Every knock-knock joke pretends someone is knocking at your door."

best_available.why: The natural hint, and the two sides really are one idea.

pairs.pair_note: "Starts with a knock" in the explanation is circular; the fix combines the two sides.

hints.reason: RAT via the Pied Piper of Hamelin and PICKLE via Peter Piper's pickled peppers; two famous Pipers. The pickle side is a half-step away (via 'pickled') but clicks.

best_available.why: Two classic nursery-lore Pipers; it's a satisfying pairing.

pairs.pair_note: It uses the same tongue-twister as PECK for KISS + PEPPER. Avoid serving both in one session, and watch boards that include PEPPER.

hints.reason: KISS via a peck on the cheek and PEPPER via "a peck of pickled peppers"; a peck is a kind of kiss rather than a plain synonym, and the unit-of-measure meaning gives the double meaning.

best_available.why: A neat double meaning tied to a famous tongue-twister.

pairs.pair_note: Peck is close to a synonym for KISS, but it is a specific kind of kiss, so I did not flag it. It shares the Peter Piper source with the PIPER hint.

hints.reason: NEW YEAR via the familiar abbreviation NYE and SCIENCE via Bill Nye the Science Guy; an abbreviation at NYC level that doubles as a surname.

best_available.why: A clever abbreviation-and-surname double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: The abbreviation is about as familiar as NYC, so it fits the owner's exception.

hints.reason: STAPLER via the stapler in Jell-O prank and BEAR via the meme "Bears. Beets. Battlestar Galactica."; The Office is mainstream U.S. TV, though the bear side leans on fan-favourite quotes.

best_available.why: Two iconic Office bits about one character.

pairs.pair_note: A judgement call: The Office is hugely popular, but players who have not seen it will miss the bear side.

hints.reason: WHIP via Indiana Jones's signature whip and SNAKE via his famous fear of snakes; one character, and the state name makes a fun disguise.

best_available.why: Both targets are Indy's best-known traits.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: CHEF via the Swedish Chef and PIG via Miss Piggy; both are well-known Muppets.

best_available.why: A fair cast-member link for both words.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant. The chef side is slightly less immediate than Piggy.

hints.reason: HOOD via the wolf in Little Red Riding Hood and SHEEP via the wolf in sheep's clothing; both are classic fable villains.

best_available.why: Natural, fair and story-based.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: BENCH via Forrest on the bus-stop bench and FEATHER via the floating feather in the film's famous opening; one scene covers both.

best_available.why: One iconic film opening contains both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent scene hint.

hints.reason: ROAD via the chicken that crosses the road and SKY via Chicken Little's falling sky; two famous chicken stories.

best_available.why: Two universally known chicken references.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: GUM via Violet's blueberry gum and SQUIRREL via Veruca and the nut-sorting squirrels (book and 2005 film); the squirrel side is softer for fans of the 1971 film, which used geese.

best_available.why: Two memorable kid-comeuppance scenes from one story.

pairs.pair_note: The squirrel side depends on which version a player knows, but it is correct.

hints.reason: HORSESHOE and RABBIT (via the rabbit's foot) are both classic good-luck charms; a clean shared property.

best_available.why: The obvious shared property; fair and natural.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant rather than surprising.

hints.reason: CACTUS via Arizona's saguaros and TEA via AriZona iced tea; a place and a brand share one name.

best_available.why: A fun state-and-brand double that U.S. players will know.

pairs.pair_note: Strong for a U.S. audience.

hints.reason: GOLF via Scotland as golf's birthplace and LOCH NESS via its Scottish home; straightforward geography.

best_available.why: Fair and accurate; it is the natural link.

pairs.pair_note: A bit plain, but correct.

hints.reason: BEE via the buzzing sound and TOY via Buzz Lightyear from Toy Story; a sound and a character share one word.

best_available.why: A sound-and-character double meaning, in the spirit of TOY + DINOSAUR -> REX.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: COFFEE via roasted beans and COMEDY via a celebrity roast; a clean double meaning.

best_available.why: A crisp double meaning with nice misdirection.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.
